To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the competition between α-decays and proton radioactivity in spherical nuclei is investigated in detail within the GLDM.
we have developed a generalized liquid drop approach to describe the competition between α and proton radioactivity in the proton range from Z=51-83.
the GLDM combined with the WKB method and relativistic mean field can describe the half-lives for α decay and proton radioactivity of nuclei with Z = 51 to Z = 83.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the α and proton decay half-lives of some spherical nuclei in the range Z = 49–83.
a unified treatment of the two decay processes.
the study of competition between α-decays and proton emissions within the GLDM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GLDM is able to describe the α-decay half-lives and proton radioactivity of nuclei with the proton number Z = 51-83.
the α-decay half-lives are generally overestimated by the GLDM, while the proton radioactivity ones are underestimated.
the GLDM is able to predict the α-decay half-lives and proton radioactivity with good accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GLDM is an appropriate tool to investigate the α-decay half-lives for nuclei in the proton number range Z = 40–100.
the GLDM can be applied to the description of both α-decay half-lives and proton radioactivity.
the GLDM can be used to describe both the α and proton emission in the same theoretical frame.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the nuclei in the proton radioactivity region, the GLDM is a reliable and effective tool for the study of the α and proton emission.
the α-decay half-lives are shorter than the proton radioactivity half-life for most nuclei in the proton radioactivity region.
